nodes.name: Yamamoto coupling
nodes.procedure: 4-bromo-2,6-lutidine (4.60 g, 25.0 mmol), NiBr2(PPh3)2 (5.58 g, 7.5 mmol), Zn powder (2.50 g, 38.0 mmol) and Et4NI (6.42 g, 25.0 mmol) were mixed and refluxed in super dry-THF solution (15 mL) for 24 h under Ar atmosphere. After cooling to room temperature, the mixture was filtrated, and then the solvent was evaporated to obtain a crude residue. The residue was treated with 10% aqueous solution of ethylenediamine and then extracted CH2Cl2. An aqueous solution of HCl (1 M) was added to the organic layer. After separation, the aqueous layer was treated with an aqueous solution of NaOH (1 M). When the extraction (CH2Cl2) was dried over MgSO4 and evaporated, the residue was further purified by column chromatography (EA:PE = 1:2) to give the model compound as a white solid.
nodes.source_text: TMBP monomer was synthesized according to the literature procedure... to give the model compound as a white solid.

nodes.name: Knoevenagel condensation
nodes.procedure: A Pyrex tube was filled with TMBP (84.92 mg, 0.4 mmol), BPy-DA (169.8 mg, 0.8 mmol), benzoic acid (9.8 mg, 0.08 mmol) and benzoic anhydride (181.0 mg, 0.8 mmol) sequentially (molar ratio 1/2/2/0.2). The mixture was degassed through three freeze–pump–thaw cycles. After gradual warm up to room temperature, the tube was placed in an oven and heated at 180 °C for 3 days. The bulk monolith was then soaked in a mixture of 1 M aq. NaOH and methanol (v/v = 1/1) for 24 h. The solid was cracked into powder by a hammer and ground by a mortar. The obtained powder was subsequently fluxed with acetone/methanol (v/v = 1/1) in a Soxhlet extractor for 12 h. After drying under a dynamic vacuum at room temperature overnight, the highly crystalline COF-205 with sql topology was obtained as yellow powder.

nodes.name: Ru anchoring and electrochemical activation
nodes.procedure: COF-205 (100 mg), RuCl3 (30 mg), 15 mL deionized water and 5 mL THF were evenly distributed in a 20 mL Pyrex vial by ultrasonic treatment. The mixture was heated in a 90 °C oven for 6 h. After cooling down to room temperature, the obtained powder was sequentially washed with deionized water and ethanol. After drying under a dynamic vacuum at room temperature overnight, the black powder was collected (COF-205·RuOxCly). The collected powder was dispersed to a fluorine-doped tin oxide-coated glass electrode and underwent 200 CV cycles at a range of 1.24~1.64 V (vs. RHE) under 0.5 M H2SO4 electrolyte, confirming the conversion from the initial Ru–Cl bonds into Ru–O bonds to form COF-205-Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD patterns of COF-205-Ru show dominant diffraction peaks at 4.59°, 6.45°, 9.15° and 26.21° assigned to (110), (200), (220) and (001) facets with no obvious change after Ru introduction, consistent with AA stacking model.
nodes.evidence_snippet: PXRD of COF-205 shown in Supplementary Fig. 7 indicates the disappearance of diffraction peaks for monomers... no obvious change of diffraction peaks is observed after the introduction of Ru into the COF-205 frameworks.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR shows disappearance of C=O at 1700 cm⁻¹ and C-H at 2916 cm⁻¹, new peaks at 961 cm⁻¹ (trans-CH=CH) and 1631 cm⁻¹ (C=C) confirming sp²-carbon linkage formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The disappearance signals of C=O stretching vibration at 1700 cm⁻¹ for Bpy-DA and C-H vibration at 2916 cm⁻¹ for TMBP indicate the consumption of monomers. The newly formed peaks located at 961 and 1631 cm⁻¹ can be attributed to the trans-CH=CH and C=C stretch vibration.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman peak at 1630 cm⁻¹ corresponds to C=C stretching vibration confirming vinyl linkage formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The observation of the Raman peak located at about 1630 cm⁻¹, corresponding to the C=C stretching vibration, further confirms the successful formation of vinyl linkage.

nodes.characterization_summary: 13C CP-MAS NMR signals support construction of vinyl-linked COF structure for both COF-205 and COF-205-Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The 13C cross-polarization magic angle spinning solid-state NMR (13C CP-MAS NMR) signals of COF-205 and COF-205-Ru provide significant structure information to further support the construction of vinyl-linked COF.

nodes.characterization_summary: COF-205-Ru shows Type I isotherm with pore size of 1.5 nm and BET surface area of 1200 m²/g; slightly decreased from COF-205 (1.6 nm, 1380 m²/g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: COF-205-Ru exhibits slightly decreased pore distribution (1.5 nm) and BET surface area (1200 m²/g) than pure COF-205, suggesting the successful anchoring of Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows sheet-like morphology for both COF-205 and COF-205-Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images of as-prepared COF-205 and COF-205-Ru show similar sheet-like morphology.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringe spacing of 0.482 nm corresponding to (220) plane of COF-205-Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The distinct lattice fringe spacing of 0.482 nm corresponding to the (220) plane of COF-205-Ru can be observed in high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM-EDS mapping shows homogeneous distribution of C, N, Ru, and O across COF-205-Ru sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS maps of COF-205-Ru unveil the homogeneous and uniform distribution of C, N, Ru and O across the entire sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru loading in COF-205-Ru calculated as 6.8 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This result was further confirmed by inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP–OES), in which the loading amount of atomically dispersed Ru is calculated as 6.8 wt% in COF-205-Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows lower energy absorption edge vs RuO2 indicating decreased Ru oxidation state; average valence +3.53 from fitting; EXAFS shows no Ru-Ru bonds, elongated Ru–O distance 2.16 Å (vs 1.96 Å in RuO2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru K-edge XANES profiles of COF-205-Ru and RuO2, the absorption edge shifts to the lower-energy position... the fitting results from XANES profiles reveal that Ru in COF-205-Ru presents an average valence state of +3.53... curve fittings results reveal an ~9% Ru–O bond length elongation in COF-205-Ru (2.16 Å) compared with RuO2 (1.96 Å).
